title: The Practice
author: Seth Godin
blurb: Seth Godin argues that creative work is not reserved for a lucky few with special talent. It is a practice anyone can choose: a habit of showing up, doing the work, and sharing it, regardless of how it is received. He urges readers to trust the process rather than obsess over outcomes they cannot control. Godin treats fear, not lack of ideas, as the real obstacle behind blocks and perfectionism. He insists that good work is made for someone specific, to change something for them, which makes it an act of generosity. Professionals, in his view, ship on schedule, accept that their work is good enough for its purpose, and then do it again. The book is a short, encouraging push to stop waiting for permission and start making things that matter.

lessons.t: Creativity Is a Choice, Not a Gift
lessons.b: Creative work is not a talent some people are born with but a practice anyone can choose to commit to.

lessons.t: Trust the Process, Not the Outcome
lessons.b: Because you cannot control how your work is received, you should commit to the process of making it rather than the result.
issues: scene 4: The 'CREATIVE WORK' label floats in empty space below and left of the question mark. It is attached to neither the dashed path nor the '?', so it is unclear what it labels. The 'YOU' text inside the amber circle is also tiny, about 18px or less at 1600 width. (fix: Place 'CREATIVE WORK' directly beside the end of the dashed amber path or right under the '?', aligned with it. Enlarge the 'YOU' circle and its text to at least 22px.)

scene 3: The stacked labels 'ANXIOUS / CAUTIOUS / COPY WHAT WORKED' sit across the overlapping translucent circle edges. 'COPY WHAT WORKED' spills over several circle boundaries, which makes the cluster look cramped and hard to read. (fix: Give each circle its own label, centred inside it. Alternatively, enlarge the circle cluster so all three lines sit fully inside the central overlap with padding.)

lessons.b: Creative block is really fear of doing bad work, and the cure is to keep producing, including work that isn't good yet.
Good creative work is made for a specific audience and aims to create a specific change for them, not to please everyone.

lessons.t: Your Work Is a Generous Gift
lessons.b: Sharing your work is an act of generosity, and holding it back out of fear means withholding something others might need.
issues: scene 7: The drawer drawing is broken. The lower drawer's handle floats outside the cabinet's right edge, unattached to any drawer front. The open top drawer extends sideways with mixed perspective, so the cabinet reads as a jumble of rectangles rather than an opened drawer. (fix: Redraw the cabinet in one consistent front view. Keep the closed lower drawer's handle centered on its own front, inside the cabinet outline. Show the top drawer pulled forward (offset down/right with the same width) with the papers rising out of it, matching the scene 1 drawer style.)

lessons.b: Professionals release their work on schedule, aiming for good enough for its purpose instead of hiding behind perfectionism.

lessons.t: Show Up and Do It Again
lessons.b: The practice is an ongoing loop of showing up, making, shipping, and learning, with no finish line and no permission required.
